messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content: The largest planet that has been observed and confirmed in our universe is the exoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It is a protoplanet still forming in the disk around the young star HD 100546, located about 320 light‑years away in the constellation Musca. HD 100546 b has a radius roughly **2.5 times that of Jupiter** (about 30,000 km) and a mass estimated to be around **10–20 Jupiter masses**. Because it is still accreting material, its size and mass may change as it continues to grow. No larger planet has been confirmed to date.
